title: P-CARHIT (LOG-ONLY probe, user direction 2026-09-27; H-CARSTACK-1 / H-TRAFFIC-RAM-1 evidence) - car-to-car PHYSICS CONTACTS at any force, classed per side. The T-CARHANDOVER2 geography: the client is put on a road lane far away and runs its OWN Gley traffic, the host (running its own traffic all along, with the fixture's parked cars around the spawn) walks in by road-snapped steps and both hold together 100 s - so local traffic, the other machine's traffic replicas, player-car ghosts and parked cars meet near traffic with the other player close by. ASSERT: the HOST (20 own Gley cars all run) logs at least one detailed [CarHit] contact with valid classes (the client's contacts are reported: 2 in run T-CARHIT-20260927-130900, 0 in T-CARHIT-20260927-131811); NO detailed line ever names the local driver (driver contacts are counted, not detailed). COST CHECK: 20 s disarmed, then 20 s armed, before the walk; compare the `perf` readouts of the two windows. NO save.
preconditions: Fixture save1 (host melaus, Client1; both avatars spawn outdoors near (65, -194)). Dev build (tp / tproad / traffic levers are BAMP_DEV only). 'tproad x z' (added 2026-09-24) snaps to the NEAREST Gley traffic waypoint by x/z and faces along its lane. Far point (-500, -150), about 565 m west of the spawn. Run 1 (2026-09-24 01:05) proved the OLD far point (999.7, -99.4) is OFF the Gley road network: its nearest traffic waypoint is 599.7 m away at (400, 0, -99.4) - so step 8 also asserts the snap is under 40 m. The host's steps are offsets from the client's snapped position toward the spawn (direction about (+0.997, -0.078)). Dev build with 'carhit [on|off]' (P-CARHIT readout; on/off arms the probe only). The rig has NO lever that moves a car, so a DRIVEN car never meets traffic here: the driver-count path is asserted only negatively (no detailed driver line) and read from the counters.
